body:
Owner question (post-01M1DF2RDPEVJ79366WHRNGGVP): is this innovative? is it SOTA? if not, what are we doing here?

Straight answer.

RecallSegmenter is not innovative and not SOTA. It is a reproducible rule baseline. Clause regexes and cue lists are fifty years of cheap NLP. If the product is "we split recall better than the next regex," we should stop.

The code red is also not a bid to invent a SOTA segmenter. Discourse segmentation, RST/EDU, and event-segmentation psychology already know that boundaries are uncertain. Shipping a lattice because papers have lattices would be costume.

What can be SOTA here is not the cutter. It is the thing the cutter is currently lying about:

The library's claim is Narrative Process Alignment — partial, unbalanced, hierarchical alignment of what was told to what is recalled, with receipts, not one similarity score. GraphHsmm, the signature, coverage, compression, population: those are the science. Every one of them is conditioned on the units. If the units came from an unlabeled heuristic, the number is not a measurement of recall. It is a measurement of the regex.

So what we are doing: refuse to publish Sherlock, NFRD, interview, calibration, or population figures as if the cut were given. Keep the baseline. Name it. Bind construction authority. Run sensitivity so a split that doubles visitation is visible instead of silent. Then the alignment work can be judged as alignment work.

If we cannot say that in English on the docs site, we are not doing SOTA science. We are doing a sophisticated aligner on a toy preprocessor and hoping nobody asks how the units got there.

Still no implementation. Still no slice.
